reveal.s: MP3 (formally MPEG-1 Audio Layer III or MPEG-2 Audio Layer III) is an audio coding format developed largely by the Fraunhofer Society in Germany under the lead of Karlheinz Brandenburg.
"Tom's Diner" was used by the German electrical engineer and mathematician Karlheinz Brandenburg as a reference in developing the MP3 audio compression scheme.
The masking effect has been widely studied in psychoacoustical research and is exploited in lossy audio encoding, such as MP3.
